full_judgment: 7. Leave was granted to consider whether, in the facts and circumstances of the case, the High Court Division was well founded in law and fact in maintaining the trial court's order appointing a receiver to take charge of and protect the assets and properties of the firm and also to carry on the unfinished work of the firm. The suit from which this interlocutory matter arises is pending and as such our discussion would be limited only to those facts which are necessary for disposal of this matter. Appointment of a receiver of any property, whether before or after a decree, lies within the discretionary power of a court, and this power may be exercised "where it appears to the Court to be just and convenient to appoint a receiver-under Order 40, rule (I), Civil Procedure Code. A note of caution has been sounded in rule (2) of this Order 40 in the following words—"Nothing in this rule shall authorise the Court to remove from the possession or custody of property any person whom any party to the suit has not a right so to remove". Appointment of a receiver will result in removal of the Managing Partner (Appellant-Defdt No.1) from the charge of managing the firm's business a right he is given under the Partnership Deed. So it is to be considered whether the plaintiffs have a right from any serious latches on the part of the Managing partner to so remove him from his charge of management. This question is to be determined by reference to the facts alleged on one hand and denied on the other keeping in view the fact that the suit for dissolution of the firm is pending before the trial court. Object of appointment of a receiver by Court is to take the assets and business of the firm out of the hands of all the partners including the managing partner and to place them under the court's protection and to prevent the partners from intermeddling there within any way. To carry on the business of the firm a manager is usually appointed and he runs the business under court's direction. But there is no bar to the appointment of the same person both as receiver and manager. It is the terms of appointment of the receiver which define the scope and extent of the receiver's duties and responsibilities. In the instant case the receiver has been appointed for both the purposes, to protect the assets and properties and to carry on the business of the firm in order to complete the work at hand. In the case of an injunction, it may be noted, only the person against whom it is directed is kept away from the firms' business and affairs; in the case of a receiver, as pointed out, everybody that is, all the partners stand removed from management of the firm and they stand aside only to see their business being done by a 3rd party. So it is only in circumstances where the partners have become so much antagonistic to each other that restoration of mutual trust and co-operation is an utter impossibility that appointment of a receiver is resorted to.
